purpose: Authoritative cross-reference index for this repo's design decisions and research findings. Each entry has a stable, grep-able ID. The ID appears (1) as an HTML anchor in its canonical doc page, (2) as a [ID] token in code comments at every governed path, and (3) here. To find every place affected by a change: grep the ID across the repo, OR read this entry's `code_paths` + `appears_in`.

conventions.finding_id: F-<SLUG> — a verified fact about how Omarchy behaves
conventions.code_token: Comments in code reference IDs as [D-SLUG] / [F-SLUG] so grep finds both docs and code.
conventions.on_change: When a decision changes: update its canonical doc section, every doc in `appears_in`, every file in `code_paths`, and this registry entry (incl. `related`).

decisions.title: Lightweight shell + Omarchy CLI + stow; no Ansible, no convergence engine
One convergence script (install); updates and cleanup audits are explicit operator actions
Own thin Lua/plugin/script fragments plus managed seams; never symlink Omarchy-owned mutable files
install must be idempotent (upsert_block + stow -R + pkg --needed)
Makefile is the single source of truth for repo operations (CI gates + `update` for packages and self-managed tools, opt-in `update-firmware`, and `verify` live health check); CI invokes it
uv and go are owned by omarchy's `install dev-env` path; `./install` actively drops pacman copies and reconciles to the dev-env install
Enable OpenCode's built-in LSP dispatch globally through a narrow jq delta over Omarchy's seeded user config; rely on project-aware lazy matching rather than a blanket system LSP bundle
Bash login shell (Omarchy default); no chsh to zsh
Aliases ported into shell.sh, sourced via ~/.bashrc managed block at EOF (ours win)
Secrets/host-specific values in gitignored *.local files
Carry ssh/bin/aliases/tmux/hypr-fragment/nvim-keymaps; drop i3/i3status/picom/ghostty/desktops/nvim-tree
Keep tmux (real customization); port clipboard xclip -> wl-copy for Wayland
nvim keymaps/options in a tracked ~/.config/dotfiles/nvim.lua fragment, loaded by a one-line dofile managed block in Omarchy's keymaps.lua; do NOT stow the nvim tree
caps->ctrl remap lives in the reloadable personal Hypr Lua module, not Omarchy's input defaults
Workspace app assignments as window rules in the personal Hypr Lua module
Float the Slack huddle window (matched on title) while the main Slack window stays tiled
SUPER+SHIFT+S screenshot fallback while the keyboard PRINT key emits no Linux input event
Personal keybindings are preserved in the reloadable Hypr Lua module; SUPER+SPACE opens Apps and only real Quattro conflicts are unbound
External MX Master mouse acceleration in an optional gitignored Hypr Lua module

Hyprland looknfeel deltas in the owned fragment (always-on compact look): slim window gaps, pin border_size = 2 past the window-no-gaps toggle, round all corners at omarchy's recommended radius, use theme-preserving terminal blur/opacity, and disable focus_on_activate so apps can't steal focus or yank the workspace
Historical slug: preserve personal SUPER+H/J/K/L focus and Shift-H/J/K/L swap bindings over Quattro defaults
Use a supported Quickshell workspace plugin, mutable shell.toml scalar merge, command module, and duplicate-repairing fixed-point shell.json delta
Historical v3 Waybar JSON/CSS delta overlay, retired by Quattro

Ghostty is the default terminal and Alacritty is denied: install independently guards the official Ghostty package-install and default-selection flows, asserts the selected default before package removal, and removes Alacritty's stale user launcher
Show the active Python venv name through a $VIRTUAL_ENV-keyed [custom.venv] module and managed block

Consolidate Claude Code custom config: stow statusline-command.sh, jq-delta settings.json (Claude rewrites it), pin the default model via .env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL in the settings overlay (not the UI-owned top-level model key), exclude all secrets/state/cache
Reference baseline = stock Quattro plus explicit additive manifests and the persistent package deny-list
Package/app and operator-tool curation: packages.txt restores and adds, packages.remove.txt drops, app-picker cleanup, and residue audit
Retired: Quattro owns the Zoom desktop launcher and native webapp lifecycle
Stable Brave Origin is installed and selected through Quattro's native browser flow, plus explicit MIME associations
Known external monitor layouts as description-matched Lua rules; eDP-1 remains governed by Quattro's lid and internal-monitor toggles

Kinesis Advantage360 SmartSet profile-1 thumb remap: SUPER on both bottom thumb keys (END/PGDN) for either-hand chording, Alt moved to the inner-right key (RWIN), Home->Tab, Calc->F14 bound by keycode 192 to the clipboard; Caps left as-is; layout backed up in kinesis/

findings.title: Quattro's hyprland.lua loads defaults then a reloadable hypr.* personal module; the mutable entry-point seam must be reasserted after refresh
omarchy refresh backs up but cp -f writes THROUGH symlinks, mutating tracked files
Quattro ships Hyprland Lua configuration and reloads only selected package.loaded namespaces
bash chain; ~/.bashrc sources Omarchy default then user section at EOF; known omarchy aliases
The separate omarchy-nvim package seeds keymaps.lua as the user seam; refresh backs up and replaces the entire config
Historical v3 Remove Preinstalled baseline; Quattro migration now uses stock defaults plus a narrow deny-list
App channels are Omarchy-native first: Brave Origin and Ghostty use Quattro flows, agents use mise wrappers, Spotify uses its sync-repo service package, and explicit extras stay in manifests
Omarchy CLI surface (pkg add/aur/drop, browser install/default caveat, refresh config, theme/font, update -y)

OpenCode LSP is opt-in and lazy: global `lsp: true` enables built-ins, opened-file extensions and bounded project roots determine applicability, all matching servers run rather than one ranked best server, and some require project dependencies or SDKs
ClamAV is the repo-managed on-demand malware scanner from Arch extra; signatures and scans are explicit operator actions, with no background daemon enabled
zsh vs bash on Omarchy: stay on bash (chsh->zsh breaks session; bash already has starship/zoxide/fzf/mise)
tmux prefers omarchy's ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf (XDG) over ~/.tmux.conf, shadowing it; we overlay via source-file and inherit omarchy's good tmux defaults
Historical v3 finding: Waybar was mutable and refresh-prone; Quattro retires it in favor of user plugins plus mutable shell.json
AGENTS.md is the canonical agent-guidance file; CLAUDE.md is a one-line `@AGENTS.md` bridge so every harness reads the same instructions
Hyprland matches `monitor =` rules at startup AND on hot-plug; `desc:` is a documented prefix match (excluding the trailing portname); empty-`output` is a fallback only when no other rule matches

Omarchy's `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling-cycle` (Super+/) auto-persists scale to monitors.conf only when the file matches a single `monitor=,preferred,auto,N` wildcard; multi-monitor desc:-rule layouts must persist scale by editing the user's overlay directly

Omarchy ships ssh-agent.socket disabled and never exports SSH_AUTH_SOCK; overlay adds a guarded UWSM env.d export for Omarchy-launched apps and terminals (honors pre-existing SSH_AUTH_SOCK, skips when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset), pairs with a one-time `systemctl --user enable` per machine, uses `AddKeysToAgent yes` so the passphrase prompt is once per session, and is verified by `make verify`
